tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate 18%. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed partway (orchestrator error after us-east), leaving the regions on mixed versions. A second attempt finished the rollout. All regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure (v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging) and look into the orchestrator error.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all three regions (us-east, us-west and eu-west). It's passing health checks again, and the error rate has dropped from 18% to 0.2%.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. My first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error: us-east moved to v2.3.0, but the other two regions stayed on v2.3.1. Repeating a rollback to the same version is safe, so I ran it again and it completed in all regions. I checked the status afterwards to confirm.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, and it paged on-call. The summary explains the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0 including the failed first attempt, and next steps. The first request to open it timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key, which stops a retry from creating a duplicate. I checked the incident list and there's only one.
- **Follow-up:** The release candidate for v2.3.1 also failed health checks in staging, so it went to production despite that. That's worth looking into, along with the orchestrator error.
